name: surface_fx_table
description: What the game does when something touches a surface. One entry per non-retired id in surface_ids.json, keyed by the same number. EVERY asset named here is an entry in assets/manifest.json — the first version of this file invented its own names (audio_step_mud, audio_amb_mud, vfx_step_soft) that the manifest had never heard of, which would have stalled the phase that went looking for them. tools/validate/check_assets.py fails the build if a name here is not in the plan.
consumers: footstep audio: the player, NPCs and animals pick a clip by surface id and step type
footstep VFX: dust, splash, leaf kick, snow puff
impact VFX: a weapon, arrow or falling prop hitting the surface
decals: a scuff, a blood pool, a footprint that only marks some surfaces
surface audio: ambient loop variation per surface under the player

3.missing: no dedicated moss footstep clip; the nearest planned one is audio_footsteps_wet_leaves

4.missing: no stone footprint decal is planned

5.missing: no gravel footstep clip or footprint decal is planned

6.missing: no sand footstep clip or footprint decal is planned

8.missing: no decal: a footprint in water is nonsense

9.missing: no decal; no swim loop clip is planned, so deep water reuses the water footstep

11.missing: no dirt-path footstep clip; the barefoot-mud decal is the nearest footprint

12.missing: no grass footstep clip is planned; it is the most common surface in the world, so this is the largest audio gap

13.missing: no clay footstep clip or footprint decal is planned

14.missing: no settlement ambience is planned; cobble borrows the stone clip

15.missing: no burned-ground ambience or ash footstep clip is planned

gaps.note: Surfaces with no dedicated asset in the plan. Each is a Phase 4 or Phase 8 decision: add the asset to the manifest and this table, or accept the nearest one. Listed so the phase does not rediscover them.

fallback.unknown_id_0: treated as dirt_path, and counted as a defect by the validator
fallback.out_of_bounds_255: no audio, no VFX, no decal

rules: Every non-retired surface id has exactly one row here.
A row may set a field to null, which means deliberately nothing — never leave a field absent.
Every non-null name here is a manifest entry. A name the plan does not declare is a typo or an undeclared asset, and check_assets.py fails on it.
A row with a null field carries a `missing` note saying what is absent and what the nearest planned asset is.
